title: SHAP Feature Pruning + Stacked Ensemble Calibration for Sub-0.220 Brier
summary: Two synergistic improvements from 2025-2026 research: (1) SHAP-guided feature pruning to eliminate noise features and improve generalization, (2) Heterogeneous stacked ensemble combining ExtraTrees + LightGBM + CatBoost as base learners. Both techniques are proven in recent literature and directly applicable to our current feature engine.

motivation.bottleneck: GA is exploring 3267 features but most contribute noise; best models use 55-99 features suggesting heavy redundancy in our 200-cap space

technique_1.name: SHAP Feature Importance Pruning
technique_1.source: 2025 NBA prediction literature (ACM CIKM, PLOS One)
technique_1.description: Use SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to rank feature importance across the Pareto-front models. Prune the bottom 60% of features by mean absolute SHAP value. This removes correlated/redundant features that waste the 200-cap.

implementation.step1: On Kaggle/Colab GPU: run shap.TreeExplainer on top-5 Pareto-front models from S14
implementation.step2: Compute mean |SHAP| per feature across all training samples
implementation.step3: Keep top 800 features by SHAP importance (from 3267)
implementation.step4: Push pruned feature list as shap_selected_features.json to hf-space
implementation.step5: Override feature_candidates in engine.py to use shap_selected list

technique_1.expected_impact: Reduce noise, improve cross-val stability, enable denser feature selection within 200-cap

technique_2.name: Heterogeneous Stacked Ensemble
technique_2.source: Scientific Reports 2025 — stacked ensemble NBA prediction
technique_2.description: Use ExtraTrees + LightGBM + CatBoost as diverse base learners, with LogisticRegression as meta-learner. Paper shows complementary strengths: RF captures historical player metrics, LR captures short-term dynamics. Best stacked models achieved top accuracy in all 2025 studies.

implementation.step1: Add 'stacked_ensemble' as new model_type in engine.py (CPU-safe: use sklearn StackingClassifier)
implementation.step2: Base learners: ExtraTrees(n_est=100) + LightGBM + CatBoost with evolved feature subsets
implementation.step4: Evaluate in GA fitness function same as other models (Brier + ROI + Sharpe)
implementation.step5: Only enable on S15 (wide search) initially to test

technique_2.cpu_feasibility: StackingClassifier with 3 base learners fits in 969MB RAM at n_features=200, n_samples=7067
technique_2.expected_impact: Stacked ensemble should outperform single models by 0.002-0.005 Brier per literature

technique_3.name: Capitol Trades Politician Stock Signal
technique_3.description: NBA team ownership overlaps with political donors (Mavericks/Sands, Nets/Alibaba, etc.). Capitol Trades tracks Congress member stock trades. Cross-reference team ownership trades with NBA schedule for potential alpha.

implementation.step1: Fetch capitoltrades.com/politicians CSV for NBA team owner tickers
implementation.step3: Look for patterns: owner buys before strong team performance?

technique_3.expected_impact: Novel data source not in any existing NBA model

cross_project_port.to_political_alpha: SHAP pruning is directly applicable to political_engine.py once feature starvation is fixed. Use SHAP to identify which of the 2640 features are actually predictive vs noise.
cross_project_port.from_political_alpha: Venn-Abers calibration (already in PA3) should be ported back to NBA islands. PA3 uses it for CatBoost — add to NBA engine.py calibration options.

implementation_priority.item: Fix PA feature starvation (bootstrap fix deploy)
implementation_priority.reason: Critical — PA has been broken for 3+ days
High potential, low risk (S15 is wide search anyway)
